comment: Ownership policy for analysis scope. Two orthogonal axes, per the SAST programme's rules:
control is whether a finding can be fixed in this repository; provenance is whether we wrote
the code. Enforcement follows the combination, so collapsing them into one class list produces
Matching is by longest path prefix, relative to the repository root. A path matching no rule is
an error: defaulting an unclassified path to any class either enforces a standard over code we
did not write, or silently exempts code we did.
Provenance is stated here rather than derived from the submodule remote alone, because a remote
says where code is hosted and not who authored it. The remotes are recorded beside each rule so
first_party_header_roots is not declared here. It is derived from every rule whose control is in-repo, so there is one definition of a first-party path rather than two that can drift.

Rules are required for nested submodules too, not only the root's. src/micropython declares thirty-four of its own, which is where this project's third-party C actually lives; without a rule each they inherit the fork's class and a vendored library is reported as code carrying a delta we wrote.

A directory vendored in-tree under src/micropython/lib gets its own rule, not a prefix. The recursion into .gitmodules cannot see it, because it is not a submodule, so a prefix rule is the one place this policy would classify a new third-party library silently.

vendor_roots names a directory whose every immediate child is third party and must carry its own rule. It is checked against the filesystem, not against .gitmodules, which is what catches a library vendored in-tree rather than as a submodule.

rules.note: Fork of micropython/micropython on branch usb2can-integration. The delta against upstream at pin 9cb7dff is 22 files, 681 added and 97 removed, merge base 4d80ff0, measured 2026-09-14 and recorded in planning/results/SAST-04/fork-delta-micropython.json in the SAST tree. It contains nothing under lib/. The submodule is a depth-1 shallow clone with only origin configured, so git cannot compute this locally; the GitHub compare API can, and must be re-run at every repin because the answer changes with the pin.
The bare src/libs path covers this repository's own manifest and any file directly in it. Submodules beneath it match their own longer-prefix rules above.

A fork of Wiznet's driver owned by this project's author. Verified 2026-09-14: micropython/micropython pins the same fork, so it is upstream's choice rather than this project's; the pinned commit is 6 commits ahead of kaizen8501/ioLibrary_Driver and every commit in that range is authored by Andrew Leech. No configuration in this repository compiles it, and it is not checked out here.

Third party, vendored in-tree rather than as a submodule, so the files live in andrewleech/micropython and are patchable there. Provenance is vendored, which governs the coding-standard families; control is owned-external, which is where a memory-safety fix would land, and those families evaluate the whole compiled surface whatever the provenance.

build_output_rules.reason: MicroPython's own qstr, module and pin table generation over this project's manifest and board definition; content this project's build produces, not code copied in from elsewhere.
Same generation as genhdr/**, run a second time for the bootloader's own build under mboot/.
The frozen module content MicroPython's manifest tooling produces from src/firmware and src/libs, both first-party per the rules above.
The pin table MicroPython's board tooling generates from this project's board.csv; naming varies by board (pins_<BOARD>.c or pins_gen.c) but the source is always this project's own board definition.
Same pin table generation as pins_*.c, run a second time for the bootloader's own build under mboot/.
